units.translation: It is mentioned by Herodotus and others cited in the Thesaurus vol. 6 p. 3, with or without the word ὄρος [mountain].
and the marshy reed of Bolbe and Mount Pangaeum
Thus Heath for ὑπερκότους. ἐφραξάμεσθα [excessive. we fenced ourselves in] Hermann.

i.e. purple of which there is such abundance that one may always use fresh, as Blomfield explains. διόλου νεάζουσαν [wholly fresh] explains Triclinius. κηκίδα παγκαίνιστον [ever-fresh dye] can mean nothing other than dye wholly renewed. Paleius rightly says "Literally wholly renewable."
the silver-worth dye of purple, ever fresh, the dyeing of garments
or may they perish utterly and most wickedly
how they set everything utterly badly
and for this house it is utterly badly
he reaps a wholly lamentable harvest
The scholiast explains it by κτήσεως [possession].
I will bring libations to you from my entire inheritance
struck by the god's whip common to all he was subdued
and this faction common to all clamors
for the newly seated one the all-powerful seats
so that he may become the all-powerful murderer of both of them
having set the sail she rows with loud noise
Thus from the apograph for τόπῳ [place].
I will nail him to this desolate hill
he came to the boundary hill
having chanced upon this desolate, neighborless hill
to sit upon the hill of these contest gods
having been freed from the open-air frosts and dews
wielding a well-rounded shield all of bronze
An adverb frequent in Homer, which besides Aeschylus was used by Aristophanes in a heroic verse, Frogs 1531.
he calls upon the ancestral gods as overseers of the prayers that the might of Polyneices be utterly born
It is generally used in a bad sense, evil, calamity.
it is necessary to unfold the whole suffering
the sufferings that one can neither speak nor ask about
such a calamity of suffering came upon them
who established that learning comes by suffering
he boasts that the deed is greater than the suffering
we were tending a new suffering with our thoughts
seeing around you more sufferings than the time that sleeps with us
for I cry out my own suffering
already I was prophesying all sufferings to the citizens
later they honor an incurable suffering
and she lamented over this suffering with fear
as it is possible to conjecture the sufferings
and for the one who remains suffering also blooms
I grieve at the deeds and the suffering
